endorsements.quote: At the organizational level, health systems across the world have introduced opportunities for patients, families, and caregivers to give feedback on their care engagement plans and other operational considerations that can identify potential or actual harm.
Additionally, leaders can consider utilizing patient-reported experience metrics to assess impact.

unlisted_practices: Implement AI decision support technology together with redesigned workflows that minimize or eliminate potential sources of human error.
Ensure health care providers do not over-rely on new AI technology and continue to monitor for new patient safety issues.
Generate real-world evidence to ensure new AI technologies achieve similar results in new health systems with different data systems and formats.
Ensure AI technology does not introduce or exacerbate disparities in access or quality, including by monitoring implicit biases.
Consider joining a Patient Safety Organization to share patient safety and adverse event data securely without liability concerns.
Partner with policymakers to create incentives, such as payments or resource supports, that help less-resourced organizations build infrastructure for safety technologies.
Ensure completeness and quality of the underlying data screened by machine learning alert systems.
Design AI alerts to minimize false positives and alert fatigue.

screen.reason: This is a strategic framework and commentary outlining actionable approaches and partnerships to advance patient safety using emerging technologies such as predictive analytics and AI.
